dates.note: Historic England 1359773 says 'between 1471 and 1484'. A Historic England Research Record, as a search result returned it, says 'probably built between 1464 and 1484 for Sir Thomas Burgh'. Both are recorded and neither is changed.

quotes.text: 2. Late C15, between 1471 and 1484, for Sir Thomas Burgh. Half H plan with central great hall. East wing brick faced and West wing chimneys and South gable circa 1600 for William Hickman. By invitation of Sir Neville Hickman, John Wesley preached in the great hall, 1759, 1761 and 1764. A fine late mediaeval dwelling in process of restoration at time of survey. AM.

note: Tranche 3, English medieval fabric and the Tudor house, 5 Sep 2026. ADDED EXEMPLAR. THE ENTRY IS FIVE SENTENCES LONG AND STATES NO MATERIAL, NO STOREY COUNT, NO BAY COUNT AND NO DIMENSION, so this record carries no measurements. It is kept because the one thing it does state is the plan -- 'Half H plan with central great hall' -- which is the diagram `tudor` inherits from the medieval hall and which no other Tudor exemplar in this cluster has a register statement of. Extracted twice with different queries; the second returned the header block and confirmed there is no more prose to find.
